title: Guido van Rossum's Christmas Holiday Project (1989)
explainer: Python's implementation began in December 1989, when Guido van Rossum used a holiday break at CWI in the Netherlands to build a more extensible successor to a teaching language called ABC, aimed at scripting the Amoeba operating system. He named it Python after the BBC comedy show Monty Python's Flying Circus rather than the snake, wanting a name that was short and slightly irreverent - a fitting reminder, for a lesson on learning a 'second language,' that a language's identity and its underlying design are two separate choices.
